summary.headline: Nuvoco posted record FY26 volume of 20.4 Mt and Q4 EBITDA of INR590 crore, but guided Q1 fuel cost to INR1.51-1.55/mn kcal and ~INR200/t cost inflation.
summary.overview: Management reported record FY26 volume of 20.4 million tons and EBITDA of INR1,881 crore, with Q4 the first 6 Mt quarter and a record quarterly EBITDA of INR590 crore. Price hikes of INR8-12/bag (trade) and INR10-15/bag (non-trade) were taken in April to offset fuel, packaging and gypsum inflation. Management said the hikes only just cover current cost inflation, leaving a gap of roughly INR200/t against the full cost increase. Net debt rose to INR4,445 crore at FY26-end, driven by the Vadraj acquisition, CCD and VEGL investments.

financial_highlights.change: first time a quarter crossed 6 Mt
vs INR3,640 crore at start of FY26; Dec-25 INR4,817 crore

segments.name: East
segments.commentary: Accounts for over 70% of sales; C/K ratio above 2.1; petcoke share targeted down from ~25% to below 20% at Arasmeta and Sonadih and from 35% to below 30% at Risda. East debottlenecking of ~4 Mtpa (1 Mt from debottlenecking at four plants) is nearing completion.

segments.name: North
segments.commentary: Plants running near 95% utilisation; petcoke share cut from 55-60% to about 50%, with a target of 45% using domestic coal. Vadraj capacity expected to ease shortfalls once commissioned.

segments.name: Vadraj (Gujarat, new)
segments.commentary: Clinker and grinding units to be commissioned in phases between Q3 FY27 and Q1 FY28; capex INR627 crore in FY27 and INR728 crore in FY28 (per management, largely Vadraj refurbishment).

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 blended fuel cost guided at INR1.51-1.55 per mn kcal (vs INR1.44 in Q4); Q2 expected to rise further as higher-priced petcoke shipments arrive in July-August.
April packaging bag cost up ~INR100/t (granule price moved from INR99/kg in February to INR155/kg); May-June outlook uncertain.
Mineral gypsum import costs seen rising ~INR20/t.
Total cost inflation estimated at ~INR200/t; April price hikes do not fully cover it.
FY27 capex INR900 crore and FY28 INR960 crore; target net debt to EBITDA of 2x to 2.5x during FY27.
FY27 industry volume growth expected at 7-9%; Nuvoco aims to grow in line with the industry.
AFR share targeted to rise from ~10% to above 13% in FY27.
capex_capacity: Vadraj Cement: clinker and grinding units commissioning in phases Q3 FY27 to Q1 FY28; Surat grinding unit trials commenced, 66 kV grid connected.
Kutch clinker unit: equipment upgrades and electrical panel testing underway; Kutch grinding unit civil works and VRM installation progressing.
East debottlenecking (~4 Mtpa, 1 Mt from four plants): Jojobera and Panagarh hardware done, awaiting CTO; Jajpur in 2-3 months; Arasmeta by end-2026; full completion expected by end FY27.
New bulk cement terminal at Viramgam/Sachana, Gujarat: ~1.5 Mtpa capacity with dedicated railway siding, commissioning targeted FY28.
Lead distance flat at ~325 km QoQ due to clinker movement trade-offs and rake constraints.
demand_pricing: Q4 demand improved as central and state capex picked up (~12% growth until February per management); FY26 industry volume growth estimated at 6-9%, with East and Gujarat/Maharashtra tepid for many months.

April price hikes: East INR10/bag trade and INR20/bag non-trade; North INR10 trade, INR15 non-trade in Gujarat and INR10 in Rajasthan, Haryana and Western UP. Blended realised increase estimated INR8-12 trade and INR10-15 non-trade.
Management expects price increases to hold near term if cost inflation stops; will take further hikes if costs rise again, but no size given.
Bag shortage in March and April (granule shortage plus jute bag disruption); rake availability cut from 4.5 to 4 rakes per day in March as rakes went to coal movement for power plants.
Early April demand: core East states (Bihar, Bengal, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh) good; some other pockets weak; pro-rata volumes in line with plan for first 13-14 days.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for East debottlenecking given earlier plan for end-FY26/FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Jojobera and Panagarh hardware complete, awaiting CTO; Jajpur in 2-3 months and Arasmeta by end-2026; all expected online by end-FY27 once CTO is received.

qa_highlights.question: Current kcal cost and Q1/Q2 fuel outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 blended fuel INR1.44/mn kcal (coal INR1.27, petcoke INR1.84, AFR INR0.9). Q1 guided INR1.51-1.55 as petcoke moves to INR2.01; Q2 to rise further as later-booked shipments arrive.

qa_highlights.question: Packaging cost impact in March and April, and petcoke flexibility?
qa_highlights.answer: March impact ~INR20/t; April ~INR100/t across bags, granules and conversion. Petcoke share to fall 300-500 bps in East and 200-300 bps in North, with FGD gypsum replacing mineral gypsum.

qa_highlights.question: Are April price hikes sustainable through monsoon?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is fairly confident hikes will hold near term if cost inflation stops; further inflation would be passed on, and it is not 1-to-1 pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt rose in Q4 and FY26 — why?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: FY26 net debt rose INR900 crore to INR4,445 crore due to Vadraj (INR1,800 crore) and VEGL (INR200 crore) investments, offset by INR900 crore CCD. Chairman-level comment: like-for-like debt fell ~INR300 crore from operations.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 capex and debt guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex INR900 crore in FY27 and INR960 crore in FY28; leverage to 2x-2.5x EBITDA target within FY27, with debt elevated for a few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 volume outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry growth 7-9%; Nuvoco aims to match it, with North at ~95% utilisation and possible cement shortfall in North for some months after Vadraj until commissioning.

risks_watch: Packaging granule shortage and bag availability; granule prices up from INR99 to INR155/kg with further upside if crude supply stays constrained.
Fuel cost: Q2 blended cost to rise further as higher-priced petcoke arrives; AFR and domestic coal mix targets must be delivered.
Rake availability constraints affecting clinker movement; road transport used for grinding units.
Diesel price hike risk to freight costs; gap between price hikes and ~INR200/t cost inflation.
Vadraj commissioning phases (Q3 FY27 to Q1 FY28) and East debottlenecking CTO timing.
Net debt and leverage path toward 2x-2.5x EBITDA with capex of INR900-960 crore a year.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes, capacity projects and demand outlook, but cautious and at times evasive on pricing and cost pass-through, declining to quantify price-versus-cost reconciliation or diesel impact.

Already, we are looking at close to about INR100 per ton increase due to packing bags cost increase and granular cost increase and conversion cost increase, which has happened.
And hence, at INR200 per ton with the kind of price increase, net of GST, there is still going to be some gap.
We will not drop price to increase market share.

Vadraj Cement clinker and grinding units, phased commissioning Q3 FY27 to Q1 FY28
New bulk cement terminal at Viramgam/Sachana, Gujarat, ~1.5 Mtpa with railway siding, commissioning targeted FY28

growth.why: Management expects FY27 industry volume growth of 7-9% and aims to grow in line, backed by East debottlenecking (~4 Mtpa, nearing completion), Vadraj clinker/grinding units phased Q3 FY27 to Q1 FY28, and April price hikes, though cost inflation of ~INR200/t is only partly covered and Q1 fuel cost is guided up to INR1.51-1.55.
